tagline: Omakase, ramen, izakayas and why Hong Kong can't stop flying to Japan to eat.
why: Japanese food is Hong Kong's favourite foreign cuisine, and Japan is the city's favourite holiday destination. People talk about omakase counters, ramen queues, the best wagyu, and where they ate on their last trip to Osaka or Hokkaido. Knowing the main styles, a little etiquette and some vocabulary lets you join these conversations and order with confidence.

essentials.title: Sushi vs sashimi
essentials.body: Sashimi is sliced raw fish on its own. Sushi is anything with vinegared rice: nigiri (fish on rice), maki (rolls) and temaki (hand rolls).

essentials.title: Omakase
essentials.body: 'I leave it to you': the chef serves a set sequence of seasonal dishes at the counter. It's the prestige way to eat sushi, and prices can run to thousands of dollars.

essentials.title: Ramen styles
essentials.body: Tonkotsu (rich pork bone), shoyu (soy), shio (salt) and miso are the main broths. Tsukemen is dipping noodles.

essentials.title: Izakaya culture
essentials.body: Japanese pubs serving small plates, yakitori (grilled skewers) and drinks. Casual and social.

essentials.title: Wagyu and grading
essentials.body: Wagyu is Japanese beef known for marbling. A5 is the top grade; Kobe, Matsusaka and Omi are famous brands.

essentials.title: Kaiseki
essentials.body: A multi-course traditional meal celebrating the season, the haute cuisine of Japan.

essentials.title: Seasonality matters
essentials.body: Japanese cuisine revolves around the seasons: sakura in spring, eel in summer, matsutake mushrooms in autumn, crab and fugu in winter.

timeline.event: Nigiri sushi becomes Edo's street fast food.
Instant ramen invented by Momofuku Ando.
Japanese food spreads worldwide; conveyor sushi booms.
Tokyo gets more Michelin stars than any city.
Washoku added to UNESCO's cultural heritage list.
Hong Kong bans seafood from 10 Japanese prefectures after Fukushima's wastewater release.
Record numbers of Hong Kong tourists visit Japan, helped by a weak yen.

now.headline: Omakase boom
now.detail: Omakase counters opened all over Hong Kong; some say the market is saturated.

now.headline: Weak yen
now.detail: The cheap yen made Japan trips and food cheaper, fuelling eating holidays.

now.headline: Seafood import ban
now.detail: Hong Kong's ban on seafood from 10 prefectures continues to affect restaurants' sourcing.

now.headline: Overtourism
now.detail: Popular spots in Kyoto and Tokyo face crowding; some restaurants charge tourist prices.

local.headline: Japan is Hong Kong's favourite trip
local.detail: Hong Kongers visit Japan more per person than almost any other place. 'When are you going to Japan next?' is a classic question.

local.headline: Supermarkets
local.detail: Japanese supermarkets and Don Don Donki stores are everywhere in Hong Kong.

local.headline: Ramen queues
local.detail: Popular ramen shops in Causeway Bay and Mong Kok have long lines.

local.headline: Omakase prices
local.detail: From lunch sets around HK$500 to dinners over HK$3,000.

debates.question: Is omakase worth the price?
debates.sides: Unique craft and fish quality vs a pricey trend.

debates.question: Best ramen style?
debates.sides: Tonkotsu richness vs lighter shoyu and shio.

debates.question: Conveyor sushi or counter?
debates.sides: Fun and cheap vs refined and personal.

debates.question: Tokyo or Osaka for food?
debates.sides: Tokyo for fine dining; Osaka for street food and fun.
